stories.title: In NA, Achakzai demands to know Sohail Afridi’s whereabouts
summary: ISLAMABAD: Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly (NA) Mehmood Khan Achakzai on Monday demanded on the floor of the House that details about Sohail Afridi’s whereabouts be shared.

The PTI has also alleged the detention and arrests of several of its other members, including lawmakers and ministers. “Afridi and six to seven other MNAs of the opposition party are missing since the proclamation of emergency and governor’s rule in KP.
The adjournment motion referred to Rule 109, read with Rule 110, of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the National Assembly, 2007.

stories.title: France announces curfews as government grapples with unrest
summary: France announced partial curfews in Paris and other cities on Monday after weekend demonstrations over soaring prices degenerated into some of the worst street violence in recent years.
Tourists in Paris had a taste of the disruption on Monday when they found the Louvre closed because of a small group of student protesters.

Some half a million people turned out across France on Saturday to denounce the surging cost of living, a culmination of four weeks of protests that began with students demanding better conditions at high schools.

stories.title: DPM Dar arrives in Tajikistan for high-level SCO moot
summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar arrived in Tajikistan’s capital Dushanbe on Monday to lead Pakistan’s delegation at a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting.
DPM Dar also met the first deputy prime minister of Mongolia, Jadambyn Enkhbayar, on the margins of a reception hosted by Rasulzoda for heads of delegations attending the SCO meeting.
Dar is visiting Dushanbe at the invitation of Rasulzoda to attend the SCO’s Council of Heads of Government (CHG) meeting being held from Oct 19-20, according to the FO.

stories.title: Govt slashes petrol price by Rs5.16 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Rs7.69
summary: Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: Christiane Amanpour to leave CNN after four decades as Ellison era begins
summary: CNN’s chief international anchor Christiane Amanpour will leave next year, after 43 years with the network, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters on Monday.
Skydance, formerly Paramount Skydance, completed its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery earlier this month, bringing CNN and CBS News under one roof.
CNN chief Mark Thompson and CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss kept their roles, with both reporting to Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz.

stories.title: Senate approves bill seeking blue passports for ex-lawmakers with incomplete term
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Senate on Monday passed a bill that sought to allow former lawmakers to have blue passports even if they had not served a full term in the National Assembly (NA) or Senate.

Official blue passports are issued to key constitutional, government and judicial office holders, senior bureaucrats and their eligible dependents, allowing them visa-free entry to 55 countries, including 22 European countries.

Speaking on blue passports in the Senate, Chaudhry said the number of these official passports issued in the country had been reduced from 75,000 to 45,000 after European countries and Canada raised reservations.

stories.title: McCullum wary of Pakistan’s home advantage as England prepare for tri-series test
summary: A match-winning century from Salman Ali Agha helped the hosts post 305 before their pace attack bowled Sri Lanka out for 268, giving captain Shaheen Shah Afridi’s side an encouraging start to the tournament.
Salman’s innings also underlined the importance of Pakistan’s middle order against an England attack that includes experienced campaigners and several emerging players.
The sides will meet again in Lahore on Oct 25, while England face Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi on Thursday.

stories.title: Balochistan investment forum set for Oct 21
summary: FPCCI President Atif Ikram Sheikh, FPCCI Regional Chairman and Vice President Zaki Aijaz and BBoIT Vice Chairman Bilal Khan Kakar said the forum aims to attract investment, accelerate industrial growth and showcase the province's untapped economic and commercial potential.

Zaki Aijaz and Bilal Khan Kakar said Balochistan offers immense potential for investment and sustainable growth, supported by abundant natural resources, mineral reserves, an extensive coastline and a strategically significant location.
They also underscored Gwadar Port's potential to emerge as a hub for international trade, transit and logistics and catalysing development in Balochistan and Pakistan.

stories.title: PSX dips 454 points; investors remain cautious
summary: Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) closed lower on Monday as subdued activity and persistent selling in key sectors kept investors cautious, with the benchmark index failing to sustain its recovery amid a lack of positive triggers.
According to KTrade Securities, the KSE-100 index declined 454 points (-0.27%) to close at 165,966 amid cautious investor sentiment and subdued volumes reaching 109 million shares.
However, the recovery proved short-lived as selling pressure intensified in the second half, erasing the gains and dragging the index back towards its intra-day low by the close.

stories.title: Despite growing ties, Pak-Portugal trade stays low
summary: Addressing a meeting at the Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI), the ambassador said that although relations between Portugal and Pakistan were friendly and steadily improving, bilateral trade remained considerably below its potential.
Our political and economic relations are good and growing steadily, but the trade figures remain relatively low compared with the enormous potential that exists between our two countries.

Highlighting Portugal's experience in clean energy, he pointed out that approximately 70% of Portugal's electricity generation came from renewable sources, offering valuable opportunities for knowledge-sharing, technology cooperation and potential investment partnerships.

stories.title: PRA to hold tax awareness sessions
summary: The meeting focused on addressing challenges faced by the business community and exploring measures to improve the tax system.
Delegation members assured the chairman that the chamber would support the PRA in promoting business registration and expanding the tax net.
Cooperation from the business community, he added, was essential for expanding the tax net and improving compliance with tax laws.

stories.title: Railways police, KMC register cases against each other amid dispute over road project in Karachi
summary: KARACHI: Cases have been registered against Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) and Pakistan Railways Police officials in Karachi following a scuffle between the two sides over a dispute concerning the construction of a road.
KMC City Wardens Director Saim Imran is the complainant in the case against Railways police.
Separately, an FIR against Imran and others was registered at the Railway Karachi Cantonment police station on the complaint of a railways official, Mohammed Hussain.

stories.title: What does Alberta's referendum on separation from Canada mean?
summary: Alberta is holding a non-binding referendum on Monday to ask residents if they want to remain part of Canada, marking the first time the oil-rich province has ever put the question of separation to the public.
The last ballot voters see is question 10, on whether Alberta should remain a Canadian province or start the legal process required to hold a binding referendum on separation.
Carney has campaigned for Alberta to remain in Canada.

stories.title: CDF Munir, new Saudi envoy express satisfaction at progress made under Makkah defence pact: ISPR
summary: CDF Munir congratulated the ambassador on his appointment and expressed confidence that his tenure would further strengthen the longstanding fraternal ties between Islamabad and Riyadh, which are “rooted in shared faith, mutual trust and strategic partnership”.
DPM Dar, meanwhile, underscored longstanding fraternal and strategic ties between Islamabad and Riyadh when he met Albugamy.

Islamabad and Riyadh have signed two defence pacts aimed at collective deterrence, the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Alliance that also includes Turkiye.

stories.title: Israel announces 10 arrests after West Bank settler attacks on Westerners
summary: Israeli police said on Monday that they had arrested 10 people in the occupied West Bank after settler attacks on an American photographer and a French mayor that drew international condemnation but mixed messages from the government.

Rising international attention One day after Levine’s beating, settlers attacked a convoy of European diplomats, including the French and Belgian consuls general in Jerusalem as they went through the town of Taybeh in the West Bank on Saturday.

The mayor, wearing a blue, white and red sash, leans against a vehicle as masked men intercept and surround a car at a village in the occupied West Bank. — AFP Netanyahu earlier questioned the facts behind the two recent incidents.

stories.title: CNN’s Christiane Amanpour to leave network after 43 years
summary: The 68-year-old journalist said she looks forward to new projects and will continue reporting and travelling worldwide for CNN through June 2027.
Her international interview program will transition to a weekly format in January 2027 before ending in May, according to CNN.
CNN Chairman Mark Thompson praised Amanpour as “one of the most trusted and beloved journalists anywhere” and thanked her for decades of journalism.

stories.title: Karachi reports its first polio case in over 1.5 years, bringing this year's countrywide tally to 7
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has reported its seventh polio case of the year, with a six-month-old boy from Karachi’s East district testing positive for wild poliovirus, the National Emergency Operation Centre (NEOC) said on Monday.
According to an official of the polio programme, the latest case is the first reported from Karachi since December 2024.
According to NEOC, Pakistan had recorded a 99.8 per cent reduction in polio cases from an estimated 20,000 in the early 1990s to 31 in 2025 and seven so far this year.

stories.title: India extends detention of top Cockroach Janta Party leaders
summary: A New Delhi magistrate extended the detention of two leaders of India’s youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement by two days on Monday, after they were remanded in custody five days ago.
Das and Ranka were taken into custody on Oct 14 for their “alleged repeated attempts to disturb public peace and violate the law”, the police said in a statement at the time.
Delhi police said last week they had removed the site from the list of designated protest venues.

stories.title: Punjab govt to ban 'spying objects' equipped with hidden cameras, recording devices
summary: The Punjab government decided on Monday to ban objects equipped with hidden cameras and recording devices, including pens, eyeglasses and watches.

The statement said “strict legal action” would be taken against the use, purchase and sale of “spying devices and covert electronic devices”, further warning that the “illegal use” of objects equipped with hidden cameras would result in “severe penalties”.
Taking up the plea on Thursday, the LHC directed the federal government to forward a summary to the federal cabinet regarding the unregulated import and sale of smart glasses.

stories.title: SpaceX, Tesla earnings to test Musk's AI spending ambitions as merger talk grows
summary: SpaceX and Tesla will report third-quarter results on consecutive days this week, giving investors a rare side-by-side look at Elon Musk's two most valuable companies ​as merger speculation gathers momentum.

Barclays suggested last week that a deal could be announced before Tesla's annual meeting, with SpaceX the more likely acquirer, though neither company nor Musk has officially committed to pursuing a deal.

Tesla has said capital spending will exceed $25 billion this year, and its shares are down about 17% in 2026 as analysts expect the company to post negative free cash flow of $4.92 billion for the third quarter.

stories.title: 'We never gave up': Naqvi highlights Pakistan's peace efforts in US-Iran war at Qatar forum
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday highlighted Pakistan’s mediation efforts between the United States and Iran, affirming that Islamabad “never gave up”.

Naqvi, who has been involved in Islamabad’s peace efforts and has made several trips to Iran since the war began, said: “There were moments when the situation was extremely tense, but we never gave up. “We continued talking, listening and working to build trust.
CDF Munir, accompanied by Naqvi, had visited Iran in August “as part of Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability”.

stories.title: Brazilian court gives Meta 24 hours to prove AI neutrality over looming presidential runoff
summary: A Brazilian court gave US tech company Meta 24 hours to prove that its artificial intelligence systems do not favour either candidate ahead of next Sunday’s presidential runoff, local media reported on Monday.

The Superior Electoral Court order, signed by magistrate Marco Aurelio Bellizze Oliveira, covers Meta's algorithmic systems managing social media platforms Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp, reported Brazilian outlet Universo Online.

The measure follows reporting by Brazilian daily Folha de S.Paulo, which cited internal communications indicating that Meta employees acknowledged restrictions affecting Lula's accounts while algorithms recommended the profile and WhatsApp channel of challenger Flavio Bolsonaro.

stories.title: Govt cuts petrol by Rs5.16, diesel by Rs7.69 for Oct 20
summary: The federal government on Monday decreased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs5.16 and Rs7.69 per litre, respectively, for October 20.
The latest revision comes after the government decreased the price of petrol by Rs3.93 per litre, while keeping the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) unchanged from October 17 to October 19.

On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.

stories.title: US banning Chinese AI DeepSeek from government agency IT systems
summary: The US Homeland Security Department is ordering the removal of DeepSeek products and third-party services ​using the Chinese AI model from US civilian agency IT systems, according ‌to a notice published on Monday.
The department is also banning the acquisition of DeepSeek products and third-party services developed using DeepSeek by US civilian government agencies.
Previously, ​several US agencies, including the Department of Commerce and the Navy, have banned ​the use of DeepSeek on government devices.

stories.title: SOCIETY: BALOCHISTAN’S UNENDING CYCLES OF POVERTY
summary: Some even work for food | Photo by Zaheer Baloch Mian Dad has spent much of his life ploughing fields on a tractor.

Debt, unequal sharecropping arrangements and climate shocks can trap entire families in a vicious cycle of dependence THE BOTTOM RUNG Mian’s situation is not unusual in a province where poverty remains widespread.
RESETTING THE CLOCK The 2022 floods that pushed Mian Dad into debt were not the first to disrupt the relationship between landlords and agricultural workers in Nasirabad.

stories.title: Climate exodus
summary: SOUTH Asia may see a vast movement of people as climate change makes parts of the region harder to live in.
An influx of climate-displaced families could deepen these problems.
The challenge is to ensure that people forced to move by climate change can rebuild their lives.

stories.title: How one hacker used AI agents and a few thousand dollars to break into scores of sites
summary: Beginning around October 2, Fagerland said he found about two dozen instances of Cairn being used for malicious activity, which allowed him ​to quietly peer over the cybercriminals' shoulders as they set their AI tools loose on the world.
Fagerland's report on the Chinese-speaking hacker did not name the victims, but Reuters was able ​to establish the victims' identities by independently reviewing the hacker's Cairn activity.
Fagerland said he had previously assumed ​hacker-agents would need at least some supervision.

stories.title: Kremlin says Putin, Trump and Xi could hold a three-way meeting in China next month
summary: The Kremlin said on Monday that Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping could hold a three-way meeting on the sidelines of next month’s APEC summit in China and that a potential meeting had come up in talks.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha criticised the idea of such a summit. “A trilateral meeting between the leaders of Ukraine, the US, and Russia could help end the war sooner.
A trilateral meeting between the leaders of Russia, China, and the US would do only the opposite: encourage Putin to continue this war,” he said on X.

stories.title: Sharjeel says PPP was 'last party' to support emergency in K-P
summary: Transport Secretary Asad Zamin, TransKarachi CEO Zubair Channa, Yellow Line BRT Project Director Kamal Dayo and Sindh Mass Transit Authority Managing Director Behzad Memon accompanied him.
Memon said that Sindh had made significant progress in public transport over the past four to five years, including electric scooters, Pakistan’s first electric buses and Pink Buses for women.
Memon said the Sindh government was working democratically across sectors, including health, education, transport, irrigation and local government, to improve people’s lives.

stories.title: IHC takes up Imaan, Hadi’s appeals against framing of charges in security breach case
summary: Justice Minhas questioned whether the proceedings could not be conducted through a video link, observing that the accused had been connected through the facility and that their attendance had been recorded when the charges were framed.

Azad reiterated that the appeals also challenged the inclusion of anti-terrorism provisions in the case and repeatedly urged the high court to halt the trial. “We shall see; we will let you know,” Justice Minhas remarked.
ATC hearing adjourned Meanwhile, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra conducted the proceedings of the security breach case against Imaan and Hadi at the Adiala jail, where they are incarcerated.

stories.title: Tariq Fazal rubbishes linking governor's rule in K-P to mineral extraction
summary: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry on Monday rubbished linking governor's rule and the imposition of an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) to mineral extraction in the province.
The federal government has stressed that people from K-P and Balochistan will have the first right to the mineral wealth of their province, and the money will be spent on provincial development”.

The governor defended the proposed exploitation of the province’s mineral resources, arguing that investment in the sector could generate employment, support local businesses and improve economic conditions.

stories.title: Karachi polio case takes Pakistan’s tally to seven this year
summary: Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8%, according to the NEOC.
According to the NEOC, Pakistan has conducted four large-scale polio vaccination campaigns this year, targeting more than 45 million children.
The next vaccination campaign is scheduled to run from November 2 to 8, targeting nearly 24 million children in 97 districts, including all districts of Karachi.

stories.title: Pakistan providing 'whatever support' Saudi Arabia needs for its defence: DG ISPR
summary: Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels against the kingdom.

On whether Pakistan’s support to Saudi Arabia will strictly remain defensive if the Houthi attacks continue, the the military spokesperson said all three members of the alliance were “absolutely clear […] that this alliance has no offensive intent; it is purely defensive”.
Earlier this month, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye convened an emergency meeting under the Makkah Defence Alliance and agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom.

stories.title: TV anchor Iqrarul Hassan sent to Karachi prison on judicial remand in Peca case
summary: KARACHI: A judicial magistrate on Monday sent anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan to prison on an eight-day judicial remand until Oct 26 in a cybercrime case pertaining to the alleged dissemination of anti-state content.
Hassan was arrested a week ago for allegedly disseminating anti-state, false and defamatory content on his official social media accounts.
On Monday, Hassan was presented before Karachi (East) Judicial Magistrate-I Judge Gulraiz Memon upon the completion of his six-day physical remand.

stories.title: Musk says will give SpaceX share to 'every kid in America'
summary: There are around 73 million children under the age of 18 in the United States, according to 2024 data from the US Census Bureau.
Musk owns 38 per cent of SpaceX, according to Forbes.
The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the rocket central to Musk’s Mars ambitions.

stories.title: Army major martyred, 4 terrorists killed in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR
summary: In the first operation on October 18, security forces conducted an IBO in the general area of Jattakabad, during which four terrorists were eliminated. “A large cache of arms and ammunition was also recovered,” it added.
In the second operation, ISPR added that security forces conducted a series of clearance operations in the general area of Shadi Kaur, Pasni, in Gwadar.
A day earlier, security forces killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during IBOs conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan.

stories.title: Mehwish Hayat explains why she limits her social media posts
summary: Actor Mehwish Hayat has explained why she maintains a relatively low-key presence on social media, revealing that she prefers to post occasionally rather than share frequent updates with her followers.
Beyond maintaining audience interest, Mehwish also emphasised the importance of personal time and preserving space for herself away from work and social media.
While celebrities increasingly use social media to share professional updates and glimpses into their personal lives, Mehwish’s comments highlight a more selective approach.

stories.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia ‘satisfied’ over progress under Makkah defence agreement
summary: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia expressed satisfaction on Monday over progress under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and stressed the need to strengthen defence cooperation, institutional linkages and strategic coordination.
On October 14, President Asif Ali Zardari received Dr Albugamy’s credentials at Aiwan-e-Sadr, reaffirming Pakistan’s commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security and defence.

In September, senior military commanders from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye met in Riyadh to review the regional security situation and discuss intelligence sharing, military coordination and the integration of defence capabilities.

stories.title: SHC rejects state appeal challenging Mahrang's acquittal in terrorism, sedition case
summary: The Sindh High Court (SHC) on Monday dismissed a provincial government appeal challenging the acquittal of Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC) leader Mahrang Baloch in an incitement case, declaring the appeal not maintainable.
During today's hearing, the high court questioned the prosecution's authority to challenge the acquittal, observing that the original complainant in the case was a private individual.
The bench questioned how the prosecution could independently file an appeal against the acquittal when the case had been lodged by a private complainant.

stories.title: UN agency to end monthly aid to 500,000 people in Gaza over funding shortfall
summary: With the cutbacks, 1.1 million Palestinians in Gaza — still about half the population — will be receiving either food or cash assistance each month from the UN agency, in reduced amounts.

The World Food Programme (WFP) said its efforts had mitigated the effects during a famine last year in Gaza and warned that conditions had not improved to the point that it can take away aid. “People are not safe.
According to the latest assessments, 1.4 million people — or two-thirds of Gaza’s population — are still “acutely food insecure” and need humanitarian assistance to survive, he said.
